### 💡 Codex Review

https://github.com/develmax/Erlang.Net/blob/af74aa110130d2937ffca262d73c297f0fd95343/tools/Native/Erlang.NifLinuxCallbackObservations/prepare.py#L20-L23
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Update dynamically constructed paths in the Linux callback pipeline**

The Linux callback pipeline still constructs flat tool paths: `.github/workflows/nif-linux-callback17.yml` invokes `tools/$tool/build-native.py` and `tools/$tool/collect.py` at lines 79 and 84, and `prepare.py` constructs `R/'tools'/toolname` at line 27. Both selected observer directories now exist only under `tools/Native` (confirmed by repository-wide search). Consequently, the workflow cannot acquire its fixtures, and fixing those workflow paths alone still leaves preparation failing with `FileNotFoundError` when reading the manifests. Update these dynamic paths alongside the explicit paths migrated here.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L1-L1](https://github.com/develmax/Erlang.Net/blob/af74aa110130d2937ffca262d73c297f0fd95343/AGENTS.md#L1-L1)

---

https://github.com/develmax/Erlang.Net/blob/af74aa110130d2937ffca262d73c297f0fd95343/tools/Native/Erlang.NifOrdinaryLoaderObservations/run.py#L4
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Migrate the ordinary-loader observer's dependency search paths**

When the ordinary-loader regression runner receives valid inputs, its dependency setup still inserts `R/'tools'/tool` into `sys.path` for all three helpers. Those directories have moved into `Native`, `Distribution`, and `Runtime`, so the subsequent imports fail before any loader regression executes; reproducing this import setup yields `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'common'`. Update the dynamically constructed helper paths as well as the repository-root calculation.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L1-L1](https://github.com/develmax/Erlang.Net/blob/af74aa110130d2937ffca262d73c297f0fd95343/AGENTS.md#L1-L1)

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve host error-handler arguments when capturing parser failures**

When a registered C# error handler calls `list_to_integer` or `binary_to_integer` with invalid input, this replacement loses the handler's saved arguments from the resulting stack. `EnterHostErrorHandler` stores them in `HostHandlerArguments`, and the previous `CaptureNativeFailure` path preserves them through `RuntimeExceptionCapture.Call`; `CaptureErrorStack` instead emits only `frame.Arity` for caller frames. Because the new exception sets `ExplicitStackTrace`, the outer handler capture cannot repair it. Preserve the existing caller-frame capture behavior while adding the short/long parser source metadata, or teach the shared helper to retain host-handler arguments.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Findings.Body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle imported flat maps with a different atom ordering**

When a flat map is constructed in one runtime (or the host registry) and passed to another runtime whose atom registration order differs, admitting its names here leaves `MapTerm.FlatKeys426` in the original table's order. Calling `erts_debug:copy_shared/2` on that imported map then reaches `DebugSharingCopy425.CopyMap`, which passes the original key tuple to the `MapTerm` constructor; that constructor re-sorts using the destination table and throws `ArgumentException` because the orders disagree. For example, constructing a two-atom-key map after registering `a` then `b`, and importing it into a VM that registered `b` then `a`, triggers this regression. Account for destination-specific flat-key ordering during import or copying so valid imported maps remain copyable.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
